discovery: Quantum interfaces between light and matter as the foundation of quantum networks

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austria

motivation: Cirac and Zoller, with Kimble, proposed in 1997 that quantum states could be transferred coherently between distant atoms by photons in high-finesse cavities. They also gave the theory of quantum repeaters and of DLCZ-type entanglement distribution between atomic ensembles, which together set out how a quantum internet could be built. Kimble's pioneering cavity-QED experiments made this programme a laboratory reality: the strong coupling of single atoms and photons, single-photon sources, heralded entanglement between remote atomic ensembles, and the reversible mapping of photonic entanglement into and out of quantum memories. Together these advances turned the quantum mechanics of a single atom and a single photon into a controllable interface. That interface now underlies quantum memories, quantum repeaters and networked quantum processors worldwide. Their work founded a new field that links fundamental tests of light-matter interaction to scalable quantum technology.
